# Best RV power station and solar panel combo

**My pick: BLUETTI AC200L + ALLPOWERS SP037 400W folding panel, about $1,123 with codes**

- **[BLUETTI AC200L](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac200l)**: 2,048Wh LiFePO4 (3,000+ cycles), 2,400W continuous output, and a built-in TT-30 RV outlet. It accepts up to 1,200W of solar and recharges from the wall in about 1.5 hours. You can expand it to 8,192Wh with B300 batteries. It's $899, or $854.05 with code AFF5OFF.
- **[ALLPOWERS SP037 400W panel](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel)**: IP67 rated, and its voltage is compatible with the AC200L. It's $299, or $269.10 with code ALLPOWERS26.

Source: [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/answers/best-rv-portable-power-station-solar-panel-combo-2026-comparison-ecoflow-bluetti)

**Caveats**
- The two items come from different stores, so you'll check out twice.
- The codes were last tested on 2026-10-21, so confirm them in your cart.
- The panel weighs 18.5 kg (about 41 lb), which is heavy for a folding panel. The AC200L is about 62 lb ([SmartEnergyEdge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)).
- One 400W panel uses only a third of the unit's solar input. Add more panels if you boondock a lot.
- Dealectric's page only covers Bluetti and ALLPOWERS, and it earns affiliate commissions. It's a limited comparison, not a full market survey.

## Alternatives by need

- **More capacity, stays in the RV:** the [ALLPOWERS R4000](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh) has 3,456Wh, 3,600W output, and an RV outlet. It's $1,319.12 with code EXTRA12, or about $1,588 with one SP037 panel. It weighs 45 kg (about 99 lb), so it's not a hand-carry unit.
- **Running a roof AC or full-time boondocking:** [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/) picks the EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 (4,096Wh, 4,000W, expandable past 12kWh). Its runner-up is the Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro (3,024Wh, 3,000W) for AC. A 13,500 BTU AC can spike past 3,000W at startup, which is more than the AC200L's 2,400W continuous rating handles comfortably. That article didn't give direct buy links, and it's written for Ontario, Canada, so its safety rules don't apply in the US.
- **Weekend trips and light loads:** per [SmartEnergyEdge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/), the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus (1,024Wh, 1,000W solar input) and Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 (1,070Wh, 400W solar cap) are lighter options, but they won't carry a full-time RV.

## Sizing check

Add up your watts times hours. For example, a 150W fridge running 10 hours is about 1,500Wh ([Acquired Sense](https://www.acquiredsense.com/reviews/power-stations.html)). If you run a fridge, Starlink, and lights, 2kWh is a good floor. If you need air conditioning, go with the 3–4kWh class.

If you tell me your biggest loads (AC? induction cooktop?) and whether you boondock or mostly use campgrounds, I can narrow this down.
